//: Part 19 §19.9.2 — the bundle budgets, as a committed file so that raising one
is a reviewable line in a diff rather than an argument in a PR thread.
Enforced by `npm run bundle:check` (scripts/check-bundle.mjs), which reads the
real `next build` output: `.next/build-manifest.json` for the framework chunks
and every `.next/server/app/**/page_client-reference-manifest.js` for the
per-route entry chunks. Every number here is KILOBYTES OF GZIP (level 9) — the
thing the merchant's phone downloads — not raw bytes.
Definitions, so a number here means one thing only:
framework  build-manifest `rootMainFiles` minus `polyfillFiles`: react-dom,
the Next client runtime, the Turbopack loader.
sharedApp  the chunks EVERY app route loads, minus framework. Redux, axios,
react-intl + en.json, and whatever else has leaked into the shell.
route      a route's first-load set minus framework and sharedApp.
firstLoad  framework + sharedApp + route. What a cold visit costs.
The legacy polyfill chunk is excluded everywhere: Next emits it with
`noModule`, so a modern browser never downloads it. Counting it would add ~38 KB
to every figure and make the budgets meaningless.
`routes` keys are the URL path, route groups stripped: the manifest's
`/(app)/parties/page` is matched by `/parties`. Anything unnamed falls to
`default`.
//shared: WHERE THESE DIVERGE FROM §19.9.2, AND WHY. Both numbers below are above the
figures in the specification table, and neither gap is something a PR can close,
so they are written down rather than left to fail the build every morning until
someone deletes the gate — which is how the last one ended up a no-op.
framework — §19.9.2 says 95. Measured: 126.9, and that is the FLOOR, not drift.
react-dom alone is 69.8 KB gz and the Next 16 App Router client runtime is
42.7 KB; 112.5 KB before one line of this product's code exists. The 95 KB
figure predates React 19 and the App Router. 128 is the measured value plus
1 KB, so a framework upgrade that costs real bytes still has to be declared.
sharedApp — §19.9.2 says 85. Measured: 95.8, down from 136.9 before this pass.
What is left is: axios 21.9 (every route boots a session fetch), react-intl
+ en.json 31.9, redux-toolkit + react-redux 11.6, lucide's runtime and the
snackbar's five icons 8.6 — all of which §19.9.2 names as legitimate shell
contents — and **decimal.js-light at 11.1 KB**, which is not on that list and
is the whole of the remaining gap.
decimal is in the shell because `src/redux/store.ts` registers every slice
statically (§19.3.9 — a deliberate decision, no dynamic reducer injection),
`partyListSlice` computes `partyTotals` in its reducer, and that is money
arithmetic. So `/legal/terms` downloads a decimal library. Removing it means
either injectable reducers, which §19.3.9 rules out, or money maths in a
reducer without a money library, which is worse. It is the price of the
specified store shape and it should be re-read when that shape is re-read.
Note the general rule it illustrates: ANYTHING A SLICE IMPORTS IS ON EVERY
ROUTE. This budget is the thing that will notice when the ledger, sales and
inventory slices land.
//routes: The `route` figures are §19.9.2's, unchanged, and every route is comfortably
inside them — the largest is /onboarding/step/[n] at 51.5 against 60.
`firstLoad` cannot be §19.9.2's 230 while `framework` is 31.9 KB above the
number that budget was built from: 95 + 85 + 45 = 225 was the arithmetic, and
the framework half of it is not reachable. These are ratchets on the measured
value instead — a few KB of headroom, no more — so a regression trips even
when the route chunk itself stays under 60.
§19.9.6 item 4 asks for tight assertions on the three routes that matter and
looser cover elsewhere, which is the shape below. `/sales/invoices/new` does
not exist yet; its line is §19.9.2's, waiting for it.
//ignoreRoutes: `_global-error` replaces the whole document, including the provider tree, so
it loads a different and much smaller set than any real route. Leaving it in
would drag the sharedApp intersection down to whatever those two files happen
to share and quietly weaken every other line in this file.
